details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has reportedly raised its key interest rates by 25 basis points, with the deposit facility rate moving to 2.50% from September 16, 2026. This move continues the central bank's efforts to combat inflation, which is expected to remain above target for an extended period, partly due to the Middle East conflict and rising energy prices. Higher rates increase borrowing costs and make traditional interest-bearing assets more attractive.
title: ECB Raises Interest Rates by 25 Basis Points

details: The August 2026 US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report is scheduled for release today, September 11, at 8:30 a.m. ET. This report is critical for influencing the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions, particularly regarding a potential rate hike at its September 15-16 meeting. July's headline CPI was 3.4% year-over-year, still above the Fed's 2% target. Market participants are closely watching for any signals that could affect borrowing costs beyond September.
title: US CPI Report Awaited Amid Fed Rate Hike Speculation

details: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) warned on Thursday, September 10, of a potential abrupt market correction. This risk stems from a growing disconnect between deteriorating macroeconomic conditions, including the Middle East conflict and rising energy prices, and currently upbeat market valuations. ESMA also reiterated concerns that shocks within crypto markets could spread to the wider financial system due to increasing interconnections.
title: EU Financial Watchdog Warns of Abrupt Market Correction

details: Brent crude futures have risen firmly above $100 a barrel, primarily driven by intensified conflict in the Middle East. This surge in energy prices is contributing to renewed inflation concerns globally and pushing bond yields higher. The rise in inflation expectations could compel central banks to adopt more hawkish monetary policies.
title: Oil Prices Surge Past $100, Fueling Inflation Concerns

details: El Salvador has reached a staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on resuming a bailout program, which could lead to a $140 million disbursement. A key sticking point regarding Bitcoin holdings has eased, with El Salvador providing data showing that additions to its Bitcoin reserves since June 2025 were financed through private donations, not public funds. This development could reduce policy stigma surrounding Bitcoin's integration into traditional financial systems.
title: El Salvador Nears IMF Program Restart, Bitcoin Dispute Eases
